html:
A small island fort in the Gambia River, built in 1651 by settlers from the Duchy of Courland, a Baltic state. The English took it in 1661 and named it James Island, after the Duke of York.

For the next century and a half it changed hands between the English, the French and pirates many times, and it was a collecting point for the Atlantic slave trade up the river. After Britain banned the trade in 1807 it lost its role to Bathurst. In 2011 the Gambia renamed it after Kunta Kinte, the hero of Roots. It is a World Heritage Site with nearby Juffureh.
